A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, objectives, losses, and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original DCL/NSCL training experiments, few-shot classification results, loss trajectories, representation analyses, and MoCo experiments.

after.justification: Original empirical results remain, supplemented by ViT and pretrained ImageNet evaluations, augmentation-similarity measurements, and controlled RSA/CKA comparisons.

M1.justification: DCL and negatives-only supervised contrastive learning retain the same objectives and procedures. ViT and pretrained SimCLR models extend experimental configurations without introducing a new proposed learning method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-1K evaluation to the four retained datasets. Figure 9 covers Tiny-ImageNet, while Figure 5 evaluates an ImageNet-1K-pretrained model on mini-ImageNet and ImageNet-1K. This substantially broadens object-class coverage; v1 only cited ImageNet as mini-ImageNet's source.

E2.justification: The retained objective comparisons still evaluate DCL against NSCL. MoCo v2 already appeared in v1; ViT and external pretrained-model evaluations add settings rather than new competing objectives or baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds ViT experiments, 300-epoch RSA/CKA comparisons with matched initialization and minibatch order, and cosine-similarity evaluation using five augmentations per pair after 2,000 epochs. Appendix A also changes the stated SVHN pipeline from 224-pixel to 32-pixel crops with reduced color jitter. This reported setting change does not establish that retained SVHN experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Tables 2-3 test augmentation invariance versus global collapse and DCL-NSCL representation alignment. New ViT and pretrained ImageNet analyses test the bounds and representation geometry beyond the original configurations. Conversely, v1 Figure 8's MoCo two-way bound-validation panels are removed; v2 Figure 11 retains only its all-class classification panels.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly discloses that computationally expensive experiments were not repeated. Five-selection averaging, Table 1 standard deviations, and correlation/p-value reporting already existed. No increase in training repetitions or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 accuracies are unchanged, but bound curves are revised: Section 4.2 changes its m=500 example from below 0.45 to below 0.89, now explicitly for CIFAR10. New Table 2 reports same/different-sample similarities of 0.92/0.13 on CIFAR10; Table 3 reports RSA/CKA values spanning 0.81-0.91. ViT/ImageNet results are added and MoCo two-way results removed. The changed bounds are theoretical estimates, not accuracy gains.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 replaces the 14-times-directional-CDNV plus 28.5-times-CDNV/m bound with a bound containing additional 1/sqrt(m) terms. Appendix C replaces its proof with a covariance-based derivation and revises Corollary 1's optimization, including a constrained optimizer and zero-B case. Variance definitions are also revised, although CDNV notation remains inconsistent between Section 3.2 and Appendix C. The other theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding summary retain the same claims: DCL approximates NSCL, NSCL minimizers exhibit collapse/simplex geometry, and directional variability explains few-shot recovery. Additional experiments and the revised bound do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains the increasing training-time loss gap through greater same-class similarity and reduced cross-class similarity. It interprets the new cosine results as augmentation invariance without global collapse and RSA/CKA results as representation alignment. Section 5 retains the original limitations concerning minimizers, bound constants, and class-count dependence.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds ViT-B/16 architecture and resizing details, new dataset splits, and augmentation settings. Section 4.2 identifies the external pretrained-model source, and the checklist adds implementation and licensing disclosures. The original code and project links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Six references are added for Tiny-ImageNet, ViT, CKA, RSA, PyTorch, and a CIFAR ViT implementation. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier contrastive-learning and neural-collapse theory are unchanged; ImageNet's reference is retained and renumbered.

P1.justification: The main section structure and most existing prose remain intact. v2 adds targeted experimental explanations and a NeurIPS checklist, expands Appendix A's subsection heading to include ViT, and moves the main-text UMAP explanation into Appendix A. There is no broad narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the CDNV schematic, pretrained-model and ViT plots, and two diagnostic tables. Appendix displays are reorganized: MoCo bound panels disappear, ViT bound panels are introduced separately, and Figure 13 combines retained MoCo variance plots with new ViT plots. These substantially expand and restructure the visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Appendix C replaces v1's erroneous 1/m-squared sample-mean variance step with covariance-based reasoning, while Table 3 directly tests representation similarity that v1 left as future work. Augmentation and ViT/ImageNet checks substantially strengthen support for central claims. Inconsistent CDNV notation, stale references to the old 14/28.5 constants, and removal of MoCo two-way plots remain drawbacks, but the targeted theoretical and empirical gains outweigh them.
